title: Direct sums of arbitrary ind-constructible families
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], inherited through [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window]: $X,Y$ are separated finite-type schemes over a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ different from $\ell$, and $p$ is a $k$-morphism. Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $\Qlb$ be a fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $E\subseteq\Qlb$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, let $d\in\mathbf Z$, let $X,Y$ be schemes, and let $p\colon X\to Y$ be proper with geometric fibres of dimension $\leq d$. For $(K_\alpha)$ any family in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, the map $\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*K_\alpha\to Rp_*(\bigoplus_\alpha K_\alpha)$
is an isomorphism.

Here coefficients mean the condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to $\Lambda_X$ and $\Lambda_Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The ambient categories are the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and $Rp_*$ is the total derived pushforward of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for their small filtered colimits in the ambient module-sheaf category, and $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of complexes all of whose cohomology sheaves lie in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The family is indexed by any small set in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Properness, geometric fibres and dimension have the meanings of [def-weil-proper-morphism; def-weil-geometric-fibre; def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The comparison is the unique map whose restriction to the $\alpha$-th summand is $Rp_*(\iota_\alpha)$, where $\iota_\alpha:K_\alpha\to\bigoplus_\beta K_\beta$ is the coprojection.

proof.text: Put $L=\bigoplus_\alpha K_\alpha$ and let $c_K:\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*K_\alpha\to Rp_*L$ be the comparison defined in the statement. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](1), $L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and, on $Y$, $H^q(\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*K_\alpha)=\bigoplus_\alpha H^q(Rp_*K_\alpha)$ for every integer $q$. Thus it suffices to show that the map from this last direct sum to $H^q(Rp_*L)$ induced by $Rp_*(\iota_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism in every degree.

source.place: First two sentences and the top row of the diagram

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$. Enlarge the given fibre-dimension bound to a nonnegative integer $d$ if necessary, and put $a=q-2d-1$ and $W=\tau_{\ge a}\tau_{\le q}$. The truncation formulas of [def-kun-truncations] give $H^n(WT)=H^n(T)$ for $a\le n\le q$ and zero otherwise. For each coprojection $\iota_\alpha:K_\alpha\to L$, apply $W$ and assemble the resulting maps to obtain $b:\bigoplus_\alpha WK_\alpha\to WL$. In every degree $n$, [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](1) identifies $H^n(b)$ with the canonical identity on $\bigoplus_\alpha H^n(K_\alpha)$ if $a\le n\le q$, and with $0\to0$ otherwise. Hence $b$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. This proves the required compatibility of windows with sums by a specified canonical map, without assuming that $Rp_*$ commutes with sums. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](2), each $WK_\alpha$ and $WL$ lies in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: First two sentences: cohomology and finite windows commute with direct sums

proof.text: For $T\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, let $u_T:\tau_{\le q}T\to T$ and $v_T:\tau_{\le q}T\to WT$ be the canonical truncation maps [def-kun-truncations]. By [det-proper-unbounded-window-iso], which states the window assertion of [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window] arrow by arrow for the same $p$, $\Lambda$ and fibre bound $d$, both $H^q(Rp_*u_T)$ and $H^q(Rp_*v_T)$ are isomorphisms. Define $\theta_T=H^q(Rp_*v_T)\,H^q(Rp_*u_T)^{-1}:H^q(Rp_*T)\to H^q(Rp_*WT)$. For a morphism $f:T\to T'$ between these objects, functoriality of truncations gives $f u_T=u_{T'}(\tau_{\le q}f)$ and $(Wf)v_T=v_{T'}(\tau_{\le q}f)$. Applying $H^q Rp_*$ and cancelling the isomorphisms $H^q(Rp_*u_T)$ shows $\theta_{T'} H^q(Rp_*f)=H^q(Rp_*Wf)\theta_T$. In particular this holds for each $f=\iota_\alpha:K_\alpha\to L$.

source.place: The two vertical arrows: the natural zig-zag of truncation maps

proof.text: The family $(WK_\alpha)$ has cohomology in the single common finite interval $[a,q]$ by [def-kun-truncations], and it belongs to $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](2). Apply [det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-bounded] with this family, the same proper morphism $p$ and the same coefficient ring. It gives an isomorphism $c_W:\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*WK_\alpha\to Rp_*(\bigoplus_\alpha WK_\alpha)$. No bound on the original family $(K_\alpha)$ has been imposed.

source.place: The bottom arrow: application to the common interval [q-2d-1,q]

proof.text: Write $j_K:\bigoplus_\alpha H^q(Rp_*K_\alpha)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*K_\alpha)$ and $j_W:\bigoplus_\alpha H^q(Rp_*WK_\alpha)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*WK_\alpha)$ for the canonical cohomology/coproduct isomorphisms of step 1. Put $A_q=H^q(Rp_*b)H^q(c_W)j_W$. This map from $\bigoplus_\alpha H^q(Rp_*WK_\alpha)$ to $H^q(Rp_*WL)$ is invertible, since $b$, $c_W$ and $j_W$ are invertible. Let $\kappa_\alpha$ and $\kappa^W_\alpha$ denote the coprojections into $\bigoplus K_\alpha$ and $\bigoplus WK_\alpha$. By definition of $b$, $b\kappa^W_\alpha=W\kappa_\alpha$. The definition of each comparison and the naturality equation of step 3 therefore give, on every cohomology summand, $\theta_L H^q(c_K)j_K=A_q(\bigoplus_\alpha\theta_{K_\alpha})$. Equality on all coprojections proves this equation. The sum of the inverse maps $\theta_{K_\alpha}^{-1}$ is inverse to $\bigoplus_\alpha\theta_{K_\alpha}$, since both composites restrict to the identity on every coprojection. Thus $H^q(c_K)=\theta_L^{-1}A_q(\bigoplus_\alpha\theta_{K_\alpha})j_K^{-1}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Commutativity of the diagram, checked on each coprojection, and cancellation of its three isomorphisms

proof.text: The preceding argument applies to every $q\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] in the abelian category of $\Lambda_Y$-module sheaves: a morphism in its ordinary unbounded derived category is invertible exactly when all its cohomology maps are invertible. Consequently $c_K$ is an isomorphism, as required.

source.place: Last sentence: cohomology in all degrees detects isomorphisms (Stacks Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic)

split_report.summary: Expanded the blueprint finite-window argument into six steps. Reused the existing coproduct/truncation closure and unbounded cohomology-detection nodes, so no new nodes are needed. Constructed the canonical window/coproduct map and proved naturality of the window zig-zag on each coprojection. Added explicit meanings of coefficient, ind-constructibility and comparison notation without changing the hypotheses or conclusion. No Lean attachment was found.
split_report.blueprint: The proof realizes the second paragraph of unit sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii and every sentence of det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general.proof.md: sums/window compatibility (steps 1-2), natural window zig-zags (3), bounded-family comparison (4), commutative square (5), all-degree detection (6).

tool_uses.why: The unit explicitly uses cohomology commuting with sums and closure under sums and truncations; this existing generic interface supplies those statements, without replacing the proper finite-window route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-2b986b0b4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item and its six steps against the main-20261015 blueprint (sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general.md and .proof.md, the unit's two proof paragraphs) and every cited statement. The statement matches the blueprint hypothesis by hypothesis: Lambda=E or Qlbar via the pulled-back condensed ring, ordinary unbounded D(Mod_{Lambda_T}), any small family in Dic, p proper with geometric fibres of dimension <= d. The comparison is defined by its coprojections. No bound is added and the target is not weakened. Step 1 is det-ambient-ind-derived-sums(1) applied on X and on Y. Step 2: the map b from the sum of the windows WK_alpha to WL is an isomorphism in every degree, by def-kun-truncations and the Mathlib leaf DerivedCategory.isIso_iff (HomologySequence.lean:88-89, all n in Z; Stacks 05RT). Step 4 uses the bounded detail node with the common interval [q-2d-1,q]. I checked the step 3 naturality algebra and the step 5 per-summand computation by hand. Step 6 is the unbounded cohomology criterion. One fault, C4, repaired: step 3 needs H^q(Rp_* u_T) and H^q(Rp_* v_T) to be isomorphisms one by one, but sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window only says the zig-zag induces an isomorphism. The fix cites det-proper-unbounded-window-iso, which is in the same window unit (on route), has identical hypotheses and states both arrows as isomorphisms. I added it to step 3 uses and to proof_deps and confirmed it creates no cycle. I also confirmed both isomorphisms independently from the cohomological amplitude of Rp_*. There are no new nodes. The duplicate search across the DAG found no restatement: the window-iso, finite-window, ind-heart sums and quasi-coherent sum lemmas all state different results. The det-ambient-ind-derived-sums tool_use is on the transitive route and redundant, but harmless, so I accept it. Edge cases checked: empty and singleton families, d=0, negative or enlarged d, negative q, families with no common bounds. No SGA source is used.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
